headline: PONG gets the cabinet's voice — and its numerals
lede: The 1972 table had one oscillator but four distinct pulses, and it wrote its score in blocky video digits, not type. Pong now sounds and looks like that machine: a serve that answers twice, rally pings whose pitch rides where you struck the ball, walls a dry tick under every ping, points closed by a low clunk — and a seven-segment score face with a net-dash MATCH OVER card.

notes.text: Sound widened inside the cabinet's world: serve vs rally vs wall vs score are now four voices; per-tier character (EASY softer, HARD edgier); rally pitch carries the strike-angle aiming feedback from the last serve overhaul.

Score drawn as 7-segment block numerals on the table and inside the rebuilt MATCH OVER card; attract title is a block P·O·N·G word-mark that fits down to the 242px phone table (a clipping bug found on a screenshot and fixed the same session).

The new serve-flash ring makes paddle-hold across points legible on phones; the pad bar + QUIT chip render only while a match is alive, and pongdrive now pins chip/pill/score clearance at iPhone-SE landscape (667×375).
Harness: pongcheck 112 gates (+31: serve-once, voice law, numeral shape), 28 mutants die; pongdrive 39 checks (+13: audio-spy + phone ergonomics), 5 mutants die.
